observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a low, domed, squat animal seen from the front, its face toward the camera. A small, blunt, conical snout-head is tucked under the front rim of an overlapping-plate carapace. The eyes are half-lidded slits under heavy brows. Two thick wrinkled forelegs splay out with long pale claws. East: a side profile of the same animal. The domed carapace is made of cracked, clay-coloured, shingled plates and slopes down toward the head, which pokes out at the right with a tapered, beak-like snout. Four stumpy, elephant-skinned legs with claws. North: the rear. The dome of plates continues down over the back, and two hind legs with claws show beneath; no face or eyes. The north silhouette is visibly narrower than the south (the shell is about 295 px across against about 370–400 px on south). On every facing, pale cream wax pools and drips over the top plates.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. Domed, cracked-clay plated shell with cream wax drips across the crown. A small head with a pointed, segmented snout and heavy-lidded eyes sits low and centred. Forelegs are splayed wide, with long claws. Painterly, clean cut-out, no ground.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. A long, low dome of overlapping cracked plates, like dried mud tiles, with wax pooled over the top. The head emerges at the right with a small eye and a tapered, ridged snout. Thick wrinkled legs with claws. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Plate dome from behind with wax drips, the plates fringing down over the hindquarters, and two hind legs with claws; no tail visible and no face. Narrower and slightly more compact than the south view.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal sits in one cell beside the human and reaches roughly the human's knee-to-hip height. It is long and low and reads clearly as a plated mound with legs. At 32 px per cell it is a small brown oval blob next to the rat, about rat-to-cat sized, and readable as a low armoured critter.

edits.change: The body plan is a broad, flat, wider-than-long burrowing wedge: a low plated clay-crust carapace with a thick scalloped armour rim, and the head sunk fully into that rim so only a blunt armoured snout-plate and two small dull eye-slits show at the front edge.

The forelimbs are broad spade-like digging blades, flattened and fanned, with no separate claws, folded against the front of the rim. The hind limbs are short, thick and paddle-shaped. The cracked-clay plates are separated by seams of pale wax that run across the carapace like a dried pan, giving a silhouette unlike a shelled reptile.
Pale wax forms a glossy, drooping collar and crust around the rim and the limb joints, so the outline is broken into wedge-and-plate shapes.

The rear view, seen from behind, shows the carapace as wide as the front view, with the same rim width and the same body mass. The hind paddles are splayed outward to the same stance width as the spade forelimbs, with the tail-end plates and haunches filling the width and the eyes hidden.
The front, side and rear views share one body height, one carapace breadth and one stance width; the haunch spread in the rear view matches the shoulder spread in the front view.

invariants: plated hide crusted with clay and pale wax
cracked-clay colour palette with pale wax accents
one shared body height and carapace breadth across all facings
transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline
exactly one creature, centred, whole body visible
request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the tammuq. A squat, armour-clad burrower that spends almost its whole life motionless under cracked clay, sealed in a wax-lined burrow. Body plan: a broad, flat, wider-than-long burrowing wedge. The low carapace is built of cracked-clay plates separated by seams of pale wax, like a dried clay pan, with a thick scalloped armour rim all around its edge. The head is sunk fully into the front of the armour rim, so only a blunt armoured snout-plate and two small dull eye-slits show. The forelimbs are broad spade-like digging blades, flattened and fanned, folded against the front of the rim. The hind limbs are short, thick paddles. Pale wax forms a glossy, drooping collar and crust around the rim and the limb joints. The rear view, seen from behind, shows the carapace as wide as the front view, with the same rim width and body mass. The hind paddles splay outward to the same stance width as the spade forelimbs, the tail-end plates and haunches fill the width, and the eyes are hidden. The front view shows the head sunk into the rim with eyes toward the viewer. All facings share one body height, one carapace breadth and one stance width. Palette: clay browns and ochres with pale cream wax. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
